name: Bedeiah
overview: Bedeiah was a male descendant of Bani, noted in Scripture for having married a foreign wife. Beyond this unique attribute, no additional tribal affiliation or personal details are provided. His mention highlights a specific instance of intermarriage addressed in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Bedeiah means "servant of YHWH," reflecting a theocentric identity common in Hebrew names. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 10:35, emphasizes a connection to the Lord, although it was not explicitly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Bedeiah explicitly as a descendant of Bani, establishing a clear genealogical link. No further family relationships are recorded beyond this lineage and his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Bedeiah's significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the returned exiles regarding intermarriage with foreign women. His mention in Ezra 10:35 serves to illustrate the community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity and obedience to God's commands during the restoration period. Through his example, the narrative underscores the importance of faithfulness to the Lord in both personal and communal life.
